newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close higher on Greenspan remarks.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close higher on Greenspan remarks.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Friday, boosted by comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan overnight, which were taken as reducing the chances of a U.S. interest rate hike on May 20.

"People are taking his speech to mean that there probably won't be a rate rise at the Fed meeting on May 20," one dealer said. "That's been enough to put shares up even though the dollar was down a couple of cents (against the guilder)."
The AEX share index closed 4.82 points higher at 780.81, moving against expectations of a lower start after Thursday's Ascension Day holiday because of Wall Street's Wednesday plunge.
"After the 25 basis point rate hike at the end of March people were getting a bit worried about May 20, although recent (U.S.) data has been quite tame," said a dealer.
Some in the markets had been bracing themselves for a rise at the Fed's next policy making meeting on May 20, seen as a companion step to the 1/4 point March 25 tightening.

But Greenspan said the March 25 hike had been a form of insurance, adding that it had been a small prudent step and that there was scant evidence of any imminent resurgence of inflation. "Greenspan's remarks caused bonds to gain," said a dealer, adding this had had a knock on effect on shares.

Unilever performed strongly following a broker's recommendation and a batch of earnings upgrades following Wednesday's $8.0 billion cash disposal of its speciality chemicals businesses to Britain's ICI.
The shares closed 1.80 guilders higher at 381.30, despite being quoted ex a 4.75 guilder dividend.

ABN AMRO also traded strongly, shrugging off its 2.40 guilder ex-dividend quotation to close 1.30 guilders higher. But DSM, ex a 6.35 guilder dividend, slipped 5.40 guilders to 195.50. Other leaders showed Philips 90 cents higher at 105.10 guilders and KPN 1.60 guilders higher at 69.70.
